title: Polynomial-Time Split Solver
statement: For all natural numbers $C$ and $e$, there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a natural-number constant $c$ such that, on every input word $w$, $M$ halts within $c(|w|+1)^{e+2}$ steps and outputs the following word: if there is an $i$ with $0\le i\le |w|$ and $i+C(i+1)^e=|w|$, it outputs the self-delimiting encoding of the prefix of $w$ of length $i$ together with the remaining suffix; otherwise it outputs the empty word. Moreover, for every input $x$ and every number of steps $t$, the total space used by $M$ through step $t$ is at most $c(|x|+1)^{e+1}$.
hypotheses_covered: C and e are natural numbers
